Relatives of people with type 1 diabetes are commonly offered screening; ask your doctor about programmes.

name: Type 1 Diabetes Prevention and Treatment
blurb: Teplizumab, immune therapies, staging and the path toward a cure.
title: Type 1 Diabetes Prevention and Treatment
answer: Type 1 diabetes is an autoimmune disease in which the immune system destroys insulin producing beta cells. It can now be detected years before symptoms with antibody tests, and teplizumab (Tzield) can delay progression to clinical disease and, since June 2026, slow the loss of insulin production in some recently diagnosed children.

explainer:
Type 1 diabetes develops in stages. Stage 1 is two or more diabetes related autoantibodies with normal blood sugar, stage 2 adds abnormal glucose without symptoms, and stage 3 is clinical diabetes needing insulin. Screening for autoantibodies, especially in relatives, can find people at stages 1 and 2.

Teplizumab is an antibody that targets T cells, the immune cells attacking beta cells, and given as a short course it delays progression. Other immune therapies are in trials. Combined with beta cell replacement research, the field is moving toward stopping the disease early and eventually restoring insulin production.

developments.text: In the pivotal trial, teplizumab delayed the median time to clinical type 1 diabetes to 48.4 months against 24.4 months with placebo in high risk relatives.
The FDA granted accelerated approval for Tzield to delay decline of insulin production in children aged 8 to 17 recently diagnosed with stage 3 type 1 diabetes.
A first in human phase 1/2 trial in Padova began giving people with type 1 diabetes their own stem cells engineered to carry PD-L1, a signal that calms the immune attack (IMMUNOSTEM, 15 planned).
Kriya Therapeutics registered a phase 1/2 gene therapy trial in Melbourne that delivers insulin and glucokinase genes into muscle, with start expected October 2026.

The Lancet Diabetes and Endocrinology published DIABIL-2, a randomised trial of low dose interleukin-2, an immune regulating therapy, in people newly diagnosed with type 1 diabetes, with an accompanying review of immunoregulatory treatments.
Follow up of children with positive islet autoantibodies treated with GAD-alum found a delayed time to stage 3 type 1 diabetes.

Diabetes Care reported a case of fulminant secondary haemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis after Epstein-Barr virus reactivation in an adult with trisomy 21 treated with teplizumab, a rare but serious immune complication.
Kriya registered a second gene therapy trial for type 1 diabetes, RELIEVE, testing VV-14300.
